📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (575 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers at Google DeepMind used AI to formally verify portions of Signal‘s underlying code — meaning they’ve mathematically proven that at least parts of the encrypted messaging app’s code do what they say, without errors.
  • Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain.
  • It has been revealed that deepMind used AlphaProof Code, “a novel agentic framework for formal verification at unprecedented depth that combines human expertise with AI agents,” the researchers remarked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers at Google DeepMind used AI to formally verify portions of Signal‘s underlying code — meaning they’ve mathematically proven that at least parts of the encrypted messaging app’s code do what they say, without errors. That’s reassuring given how many vulnerabilities AI systems have discovered in software lately, and how many people’s communications are protected by Signal’s cryptography. WhatsApp and Google Messages use the same encryption.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain.

It has been revealed that deepMind used AlphaProof Code, “a novel agentic framework for formal verification at unprecedented depth that combines human expertise with AI agents,” the researchers remarked. They added that formal verification “is the highest standard of security assurance,” but, without automation at scale like AI systems, difficult and time-consuming.

AI companies like OpenAI have been on a math-breakthrough tear as of late, in some cases solving nearly century-old math problems with AI. By computing at such vast scale, AI models can rapidly accelerate much of the manual work mathematicians do.

Using AlphaProof Code and building on earlier verification work by the Signal Foundation, DeepMind researchers divided the verification task into two camps. Humans worked with agents to identify what they needed to prove, and multiple agents running Gemini Carbon, the firm’s latest model, then executed it. The agents also audited the proof and “highlighted areas that needed a second look by a human — just 1% of the codebase, a massive time savings,” the researchers wrote.

Also: After the vibe-coding rush comes the debugging hangover.

For good measure, researchers tested AlphaProof Code’s ability to distinguish correct from flawed code by showing it two previously fixed Signal bugs, for which it produced correct proofs.

Recent findings suggest that “Our work marks the first time AI has been used to formally verify a widely deployed cryptographic protocol at this depth,” the researchers wrote. “It’s also the first time the implementation of a widely deployed protocol like this has been formally verified by any method, with or without AI.”.

Normally, researchers need to manually develop a proof to verify software, which takes much longer. That labor-intensive barrier has made formal verification a distant promised land, until now. The DeepMind team’s verification took a month to do what might normally take experts years.

DeepMind did not verify all of Signal’s code, but noted that this test is a step toward improved security infrastructure at a time when AI is disrupting the entire cybersecurity space.

Also: How to encrypt emails in Gmail, Outlook, and more.

“Having the core Signal protocol rigorously verified with automated theorem proving gives us even greater confidence that our code delivers on its privacy guarantees,” the researchers wrote.

It has been revealed that the breakthrough reiterates how deeply AI is both a massive risk for cybersecurity and an equally powerful fix. The year 2026 has been especially marked by AI-related security incidents, many of which involve agents. At the same time, companies like Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI are developing models geared specifically toward cybersecurity, including Anthropic’s Claude Mythos.

Recent findings suggest that deepMind did not share any aims to release its findings as a consumer product, though the researchers are open-sourcing their code to help others with formal verification efforts. “Verifying Signal’s core cryptography lays the groundwork to secure other vital systems, from medical device firmware to power grid software,” DeepMind added.

#363. Here’s how Google’s Android XR glasses are handling the camera & privacy

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (970 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5google ↗ Open Full Page

Here’s how Google’s Android XR glasses are handling the camera & privacy

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that google’s Intelligent Eyewear push with the first Android XR glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster are forced into an unfortunate uphill battle.
  • In a recent development, to quickly summarize the problem at hand (and name names), Meta’s smart glasses developed a reputation of being abused by bad actors who would disable the visible privacy LED (which Meta only recently fixed) or use these glasses in tasteless ways.
  • In a recent development, it’s a shame, because a camera in smart glasses serves such a functional role, both for the user in just capturing pictures and for the AI assistant built into the experience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that google’s Intelligent Eyewear push with the first Android XR glasses from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster are forced into an unfortunate uphill battle. The “perv glasses” stigma is very real because, frankly, early movers in this category didn’t respect privacy. Here’s how Android XR and Gemini are handling the camera and privacy on “Intelligent Eyewear,” and why I think Google has struck a near-perfect balance.

In a recent development, to quickly summarize the problem at hand (and name names), Meta’s smart glasses developed a reputation of being abused by bad actors who would disable the visible privacy LED (which Meta only recently fixed) or use these glasses in tasteless ways. Combine that with improper handling of recordings on Meta’s part and it’s a recipe for distrust and an earned social stigma. It’s not like Google is a simple bystander here, either. The original Google Glass project was met with the “Glasshole” stigma, and it’s something that Google has clearly learned a lot of lessons from.

In a recent development, it’s a shame, because a camera in smart glasses serves such a functional role, both for the user in just capturing pictures and for the AI assistant built into the experience. I recently talked about how the camera was my favorite part of smart glasses in an issue of our 9to5Google Weekender newsletter, but how it just feels a bit wrong now.

Anyway, with that context in mind, let’s look at how Google is handling this touchy subject.

According to recent reports, it starts with the outward-facing light on every part of Android XR glasses, which works similarly to the privacy LED on Meta’s glasses. The key distinction here is this is a “recording light” on Android XR glasses. It turns on whenever the glasses are capturing content that can be viewed later in some form or fashion by the user. So if you’re taking a picture or recording a video, it lights up. If you’re just using Gemini for context, the light doesn’t activate. That’s because any camera captures being used for Gemini are deleted immediately after use. They won’t show up in your Gemini chat logs and that’s not a choice for the user – these images are purged immediately after they’ve been used so that you as the user nor Google can use them. That includes Google not using visuals from Gemini captures for AI training or advertising. Owners also have control over what apps on Android XR glasses can use the camera.

Industry observers note that importantly, the light on each pair of Android XR glasses is also designed to avoid any tampering. Android XR glasses automatically perform a system check to ensure the light is working on a regular basis – you might catch the light blinking in white and blue while charging which is a part of the system check ensuring the hardware is fully functional. If the light is found not to be working, the camera is disabled.

One of the pieces of this package that really caught my attention is how Google is handling the privacy of those around you. When your Intelligent Eyewear glasses send a photo to Gemini, your phone automatically redacts faces from the image before it’s sent to Gemini. This happens locally on the phone, essentially as a part of the glasses app. Similarly, voice data sent to Gemini filters out other voices besides your own. The voice filtering bit is just one way in which Google is doing some impressive things with the microphones here, with another example being that the live translation feature works in a 60-degree “cone” in front of you, filtering out other voices in the space.

Continuing on with how the camera interacts with Gemini, Google explained in a conversation with 9to5Google that Gemini is tuned not to use the camera in cases where it’s not obvious that the user wants the camera to be active. An interaction such as “what painting is this” would very clearly imply that the user wants the glasses to view the scene in front of them and identify the art piece, where “how much money is on the table,” Google explained, would ask for a follow-up before using the camera seeing as it’s not obvious that the user expects the camera to be used in that sort of phrase.

Sources indicate that another way in which Android XR glasses will avoid the recording stigma is with their limits. Google is limiting Intelligent Eyewear video recording to 90-second sessions. While that does limit what the user can do, Google said that most recordings fell within that window anyway. Meta, by comparison, offers recordings up to 5 minutes.

Beyond just the glasses app and Gemini, Google says it is making other efforts across its ecosystem to protect against and deter misuse of the camera on Android XR glasses, including:.

For the most part, Google’s efforts around privacy on Android XR glasses aren’t groundbreaking. This is how it should work. But seeing as the bar is exceptionally low thanks to a rough start from competitors, I found myself reassured and even a bit impressed by the messaging here – a clear explanation of the indicator light and the automatic on-device face redaction and deletion of Gemini imagery both go a long way.

Google’s sentiment around privacy on glasses is pretty nearly summed up by a sentence in its privacy post today: “…when technology can see the world around you, it has a responsibility to the people around you, too.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that kalshi and Polymarket US filed federal suits against Missouri and Louisiana on the same day the CFTC sued Utah.
  • Two more states now face prediction market operators in federal court.
  • Recent findings suggest that kalshi is challenging a cease-and-desist demand from Missouri.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that kalshi and Polymarket US filed federal suits against Missouri and Louisiana on the same day the CFTC sued Utah. The cases push the preemption fight into two states where licensed sportsbooks and casino partners stand to lose business to untaxed competitors.

Two more states now face prediction market operators in federal court. Kalshi’s case targets Missouri, while Polymarket US went after Louisiana. The CFTC filed its own suit against Utah that same day.

Recent findings suggest that kalshi is challenging a cease-and-desist demand from Missouri. The state told it to pull its sports event contracts or get a state sports betting license. Polymarket US filed as QCX LLC. It named Louisiana’s attorney general and the Louisiana Gaming Control Board as defendants.

Sources indicate that both companies make the same core argument. They say federal commodities law, the Commodity Exchange Act, overrides state gambling enforcement.

According to recent reports, missouri’s position is direct. The demand to Kalshi came from the office of Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, and Kalshi was not its only target.

The office says that offering sports event contracts in Missouri counts as unlicensed sports wagering. It also holds that federal law does not override state law here. In its view, sports event contracts are not swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act. Companies “cannot repackage sports bets as event contracts” to get around Missouri law, Hanaway said.

The stakes for the licensed market are concrete. Sports wagering became legal in Missouri through Amendment 2. Oversight of the licensed books sits with the Missouri Gaming Commission.

Sources indicate that the commission’s July 2026 revenue detail report demonstrates the scale of that business. A prediction market selling sports contracts without a license would pay none of that tax. It would compete for the same customers as the licensed books.

In a recent development, louisiana’s regulated market works differently. Its licenses go first to in-state casinos. Untaxed sports contracts there would compete with those casinos and their sportsbook partners.

It has been revealed that the Louisiana Gaming Control Board had already acted on the issue. In December 2025, it sent an advisory on prediction markets and event-based contracts. The advisory went to all sports wagering licensees and platform provider permittees.

That approach targets the licensed side of the market. Polymarket US’s suit now tests whether the state can reach the prediction market operators directly.

Recent findings suggest that the federal regulator has taken a firm public line. The CFTC noted Congress made it the only federal regulator responsible for overseeing prediction markets. Its Utah suit seeks to stop the state from using its own laws to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets. It followed civil enforcement actions that Utah brought in state court.

Companies cannot repackage sports bets as ‘event contracts’ to evade Missouri law. Polymarket, Kalshi, Novig, Crypto​.com, Underdog, and Robinhood are not licensed to offer sports wagering in Missouri. Until they are licensed by the Missouri Gaming Commission, we are demanding… pic.twitter.com/KqeH1rGjJn.

Recent findings suggest that — Attorney General Catherine L. Hanaway (@AGCHanaway) September 18, 2026.

According to recent reports, federal appeals courts are already split on whether state gambling law can reach these contracts. The question is moving toward the Supreme Court. Each new filing adds pressure on states and operators alike.

Missouri’s dispute reaches well beyond Kalshi. Its cease-and-desist letters remain in play for Polymarket, Robinhood, Crypto.com, Novig and Underdog. The outcome could decide whether sports contracts are shut out of Missouri and Louisiana.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Tuesday, Apple released security patches for iOS, iPadOS, MacOS, WatchOS, and VisionOS, which address wireless security flaws in Bluetooth pairing, AirPlay, and Messages.
  • According to recent reports, according to Apple’s security notes, vulnerabilities can allow attackers to establish a Bluetooth connection without user interaction, bypass AirPlay connection rate limits, and join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages.
  • It has been revealed that you should update your devices now, as several generations are affected across device categories.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Tuesday, Apple released security patches for iOS, iPadOS, MacOS, WatchOS, and VisionOS, which address wireless security flaws in Bluetooth pairing, AirPlay, and Messages.

According to recent reports, according to Apple’s security notes, vulnerabilities can allow attackers to establish a Bluetooth connection without user interaction, bypass AirPlay connection rate limits, and join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages. Around half of these flaws were found internally by Apple, while the others were submitted by researchers.

It has been revealed that you should update your devices now, as several generations are affected across device categories. The following software versions include patches:.

Apple’s security notes list a fix for Messages to prevent attackers from remotely joining an iMessage group chat and reading its messages. According to Apple, “an authorization glitch was addressed with improved validation” to fix the issue.

There was likely a flaw in Apple’s iMessage authorization logic that allowed an unauthorized user to inject themselves into a group chat roster without permission from an existing member.

Also: Your iPhone can spot scams for you with iOS 27.

Another concern in Messages could allow an authorized added member to access messages within a group chat that were sent before they joined. According to Apple, the code that caused this issue has been removed.

One security fix across devices and software versions addresses an issue where a malicious actor could establish a Bluetooth connection to your device without user interaction.

Apple was not specific about which kind of Bluetooth attack this fix addresses; however, it’s reminiscent of Bluetooth Low Energy Re-Pairing vulnerabilities found earlier this year by French researchers.

This study explains how bad actors can exploit vulnerabilities in Bluetooth Low Energy pairing logic to execute one-click or zero-click impersonation and man-in-the-middle attacks against unsuspecting devices, regardless of Bluetooth version or security level.

Also: Beware of Bluetooth sniffers: Your favorite gadgets could expose you.

Recent findings suggest that the study was published in January of this year, and the researchers reported initial findings to Apple, which “[appeared] to have hardened the re-pairing logic in MacOS/iOS 26,” according to the study. It’s possible that Apple internally found another vulnerability in the same Bluetooth pairing logic, given how many devices across Bluetooth versions are affected.

According to Apple, this concern was fixed with “improved checks,” likely meaning strengthened verification steps during pairing.

Sources indicate that another vulnerability pertains to AirPlay, allowing an attacker within Bluetooth range or on the same network to bypass the rate limit on AirPlay pairing code attempts. This issue also affects iOS, iPadOS, MacOS, VisionOS, and WatchOS.

This vulnerability is similar to the AirBorne attack method. This report, published in 2025 by Oligo, describes how zero-click remote code execution, user-interaction bypass, denial-of-service, man-in-the-middle, and other techniques can be used to take control of a device that supports AirPlay.

However, the current security issue is likely less serious or far-reaching and was discovered internally.

For this issue, when you pair a device with an AirPlay receiver, such as an Apple TV, AirPlay-enabled TV, or Mac, it will prompt you for a security PIN to verify your device. You can only input an incorrect PIN a certain number of times before you’re denied pairing for a period of time.

Also: The upcoming Apple TV 4K is always listening for ‘Hey Siri’.

According to recent reports, A vulnerability in this defense mechanism can allow an attacker within Bluetooth range of, or on the same network as, your device to use a brute-force attack, bypassing the mechanism that limits the number of incorrect PIN attempts, and eventually gain access to your device. There are only so many PIN combinations.

According to Apple, “a logic glitch was addressed with improved state management” to fix this problem.

Google is finally introducing a “Hey Gemini” hotword for its AI assistant, but it’s only on Android XR glasses to start.

Industry observers note that around a decade after “Hey Google” made its debut, Google is introducing its first upcoming always-listening hotword. “Hey Gemini” makes its debut on Google’s Intelligent Eyewear glasses powered by Android XR, with wearers able to use that hotword in place of “Hey Google.”.

This is a move that doesn’t come as a huge surprise. If anything, it’s perhaps a bit overdue.

The move from Assistant to Gemini would have been the expected place for Google to make this change, but it’s one that many will certainly welcome. While the hotword you use really won’t matter much at the end of the day, “Hey Google” has been recognized by many to not roll of the tongue very nicely. It’s a phrase that’s easy to stumble over, where “Hey Gemini” is a bit smoother.

As for whether or not “Hey Gemini” will become the default on future product remains unclear, but it’s a change only available on glasses for now.

We’ve asked Google if both hotwords will be active on Android XR glasses, but it was implied that this is, in fact, the case. When paired to Samsung glasses, “Hey Bixby” may also be in play, as Samsung’s voice assistant is supported on Intelligent Eyewear. Exact functionality, though, is something we’re still waiting for more clarity on.

  • This happens quite often when I’m viewing content in the Google News app — especially in the morning, when my eyes are still in “wake up” mode.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How many times have you been on your phone, wanted to read something (a piece of news, a website, etc.), only to find the text is too small and every effort to zoom in doesn’t work?

Also: 7 Android accessibility features that can make your life easier.

This happens quite often when I’m viewing content in the Google News app — especially in the morning, when my eyes are still in “wake up” mode. It can be frustrating. And it’s not only text. Sometimes there’s an image I need to enlarge, but for whatever reason, pinch-to-zoom isn’t working on that particular screen.

Fortunately, there’s an option you can enable to ensure you can always zoom in on your Android device, no matter what’s on the screen. The option is found in Accessibility and is aptly called Magnification. With this feature enabled, you can swiftly zoom in on the screen to enlarge any displayed content. It doesn’t matter what’s on the screen or what app is showing the image, page, or text — Magnification will magnify it.

Recent findings suggest that this iteration of the feature has been available since Android 15. I found it by accident while poking around the Settings page. Since then, I’ve used it quite a bit, and it’s eased my morning frustration with reading news sites.

The Magnification feature is quite simple: once enabled, a magnifier shortcut appears on the screen. Tap that button, and whatever is on your screen will increase in size. It’s really that easy. One caveat: As long as the Magnification shortcut is enabled, the button remains on your screen. You can move the button up and down or to the left or right side of the display, but if you want the feature enabled, the button must remain.

Industry observers note that the good news, however, is that the button does fade a bit, so it’s not glaring and in your face. You can still see it, but it gets just enough transparency that it doesn’t stand out all that much.

Also: Android is getting my favorite iOS tracking feature.

OK, let’s enable Magnification.

Open Settings by dragging the Notification Shade down twice, then tapping the gear icon (or tapping Settings in the App Drawer). Where this is located depends on the Android version you’re using and your device. For example, on my Pixel 9 Pro, it’s in Settings > Accessibility > Magnification. On a RedMagic 12 Pro, it’s in Settings > Features > Accessibility. If you don’t find it right away, open Settings and search for Magnification.

In a recent development, once you’ve found the Magnification option, tap the On/Off slider until it’s in the On position, and the Magnifier button will appear on your screen. Tap the button, and whatever is on the display will enlarge enough that you shouldn’t have any trouble reading it.

Industry observers note that here’s a little tip: After tapping the Magnification button, whatever’s been enlarged can be scrolled vertically, but not horizontally. Fortunately, there’s a way to ensure that you can read everything on the page.

Also: I use Google Magnifier to read tiny print without my glasses.

Recent findings suggest that tap the gear icon at the bottom right of the display to open the options pop-up. On this page, tap the “Magnifier size” icon that’s second from the right. This enables a movable magnifier you can place where you need it (kind of like a traditional magnifying glass). You can also change the size of the movable magnifier (by tapping one of the other “Magnifier size” buttons) as well as the size of the text when magnified (by dragging the bottom slider).

Also: RedMagic 12 Pro is the fastest Android phone I’ve ever seen.

This feature has alleviated the early-morning frustration of having to squint (even with my glasses on) to read certain news sites. Give it a try and see if it doesn’t make your Android life a bit clearer.

In a recent development, shahram Izadi, VP and GM of XR, explains how we are building privacy protections into intelligent eyewear to safeguard both wearers and bystanders. These features include physical indicator lights, automatic face redaction, and strict data encryption to ensure your information remains secure. You can visit the Google Safety Center to learn more about our approach to privacy and how we handle data across our wearable devices.

In a recent development, shahram Izadi, VP and GM of XR, explains that our intelligent eyewear uses Gemini to help you translate signs, read menus, and navigate your day. We built these glasses with privacy for everyone in mind, including physical indicator lights for bystanders and automatic face redaction. Your visual data is encrypted, never used for ads, and not saved in your history. You also keep full control over your settings and can turn the device off anytime.

According to recent reports, intelligent eyewear with Gemini 1 can help you understand another language, make sense of a confusing parking sign, or know when to take the next step in your recipe, all thanks to its ability to see what you see. And with experiences like Guided Vision in Gemini Live, these glasses can provide audio descriptions to people who are blind or have low vision as they read small print or find everyday items. 2.

But when technology can see the world around you, it has a responsibility to the people around you, too.

Throughout our years of research on glasses, we listened closely to wearers, bystanders, and privacy experts. We found that wearers were constantly calculating using glasses like these out-and-about during their day, while bystanders noted concerns about being filmed without their knowledge. This led us to the conviction that privacy protections on glasses must cover both the person behind the lenses and those in front of them.

In a recent development, with this in mind, we set out to design the glasses so that personal help doesn’t come at the expense of anyone’s privacy. Here are some of the key features we’ve built into both the hardware and software to protect wearers and those nearby.

It has been revealed that these are a few examples of the privacy features built into the intelligent eyewear experience. Learn more about our approach in the Google Safety Center.

In addition to these features, there are also protections across Google apps and services to deter misuse of the glasses.

This is just the beginning. Privacy is foundational to how we design, build, and evolve wearable technology. As glasses become more capable, our focus is on creating helpful experiences that make both wearers and bystanders feel protected. We look forward to advancing this work in collaboration with privacy experts and others across the ecosystem to further protections for everyone on both sides of the lens.

According to recent reports, rush Street Interactive kept its 2026 revenue guidance but stated October trading points to the low end of the range, after raising its outlook a quarter earlier. With online casino at 75% of revenue, the warning is fresh operator evidence that US online casino growth is cooling heading into the fourth quarter.

According to recent reports, the third-quarter results of BetRivers owner Rush Street Interactive came out on October 28. The guidance range it reaffirmed implies 38% to 41% growth for 2026. Adjusted EBITDA guidance stays at $245 million to $265 million, with October tracking toward the midpoint of that range.

The warning breaks a pattern from the summer. In the second quarter, reported July 29, the company posted record revenue of $393.8 million, up 46%, and raised its full-year guidance. Third-quarter sales were up from $277.9 million a year earlier but below the second-quarter total. Growth also slowed from the 46% pace of the prior quarter.

In a recent development, net income rose 93% to $28.7 million, from $14.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose 73% to $62.2 million, from $36.0 million. Sales and marketing expense grew 43% to $56.0 million, from $39.0 million a year earlier.

Industry observers note that the online casino share of revenue rose from 72% in the second quarter. That weighting makes the company a close read on US casino demand. The 32% growth in casino revenue also includes Latin America, so it is not a pure US figure.

Sources indicate that player numbers kept growing. North American monthly active consumers reached a record 300,572, up 34% year over year. Latin American users rose 46% to 607,308, for a total of 907,881.

It has been revealed that management blamed slower growth in the North American online casino market, not lost market share, for revenue tracking toward the low end of guidance. Michigan, in their view, has also become more competitive. Statewide figures from Michigan are consistent with a softer market. In September, Michigan iGaming adjusted gross receipts came to $288.15 million, 0.9% lower than in August.

According to recent reports, the shares fell 1.82% in regular trading on October 28 to $15.13. After hours, the stock moved below its 52-week low. The tech giant bought back about $14 million of stock during the quarter and another $11 million after it ended. That leaves $75 million under its repurchase authorization.

Rush Street Interactive reported third-quarter revenue up 39% to $385.9 million, but North American revenue rose only 14% and it says October trends point to the low end of its revenue guidance. pic.twitter.com/DYpJ8f2Z3a.

— iGaming Times (@igaming_times) October 29, 2026.

The outlook carries conditions. It covers only markets that are already live. It also assumes current tax structures stay in place, including Colombia’s temporary 16% excise tax through year-end.

That leaves the fourth quarter as the test of the low-end warning. Investing.com calculated that the reiterated full-year guidance implies fourth-quarter revenue of roughly $410 million to $450 million.

Sources indicate that android XR glasses get their own control wearable, but you might already own it. Google states the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch will be able to control Android XR glasses.

Google just launched its line of Intelligent Eyewear glasses. The smart glasses run on Android XR with hardware built by Samsung. They start at $395, with pre-orders opening up today through both Warby Parker and Gentle Monster.

For all the smart features they have, one of the best might be the sly integration Google is setting up between Intelligent Eyewear and its existing wearables. Google quietly noted that both Pixel Watch models and the Fitbit Air will be able to control Android XR glasses, like a dedicated control band some competitor smart glasses come with.

Industry observers note that pixel Watch already supports gesture controls using sensors to detect movements like finger pinching or wrist adjustments. Google’s Android XR demo included pausing and playing music using a pinch gesture. We imagine gesture controls will support as much as the touchpad that sits in the arms of Intelligent Eyewear models, though it’s not clear what gestures will be supported just yet. You’ll still be able to use the touch sensors, but Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air will be just another avenue.

In a recent development, according to what Google told us, the Pixel Watch will be supported around launch, with Fitbit Air adding support sometime in 2027. Galaxy Watch will also be supported on Samsung devices. Considering the Fitbit Air is reportedly such a massive hit that Google is having a hard time keeping up, the move only makes sense. The Fitbit Air is also only $99, whereas something like Meta’s Neural Band goes for $199.

AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Microsoft fixes over 1,000 Windows flaws – and one is being exploited

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1106 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Windows 11 customers who’ve struggled to navigate and use the right-click menu in File Explorer now finally have some relief.
  • As usual, the monthly patch is mandatory, which means it should automatically download and install on your PC.
  • Also: You can change Windows settings directly from a search now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Windows 11 customers who’ve struggled to navigate and use the right-click menu in File Explorer now finally have some relief. With the November Patch Tuesday Windows update, you’re now able to customize the menu to add and remove specific commands and apps so that only your favorites appear.

As usual, the monthly patch is mandatory, which means it should automatically download and install on your PC. To check, head to Settings and select Windows Update. If the latest update — labeled “2026-11 Security Update (KB5132061) (26300.9974)” -– pops up as installed with a pending restart, just reboot your computer. Otherwise, click the button to check for updates and allow it to download and install.

Also: You can change Windows settings directly from a search now.

One caveat: Microsoft’s monthly updates fully support Windows 11 26H2 and 25H2. But support for 24H2 ended last month, at least for the Home and Pro editions. Windows 11 24H2 Enterprise and Education will continue to get monthly security updates, though not regular non-security preview updates, while Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education will receive no more updates after this month.

If you use Windows 11 Home or Pro, be sure you upgrade your system to 26H2 to continue receiving the necessary support and updates.

First and foremost in the latest upgrade is the new customizable right-click menu.

Sources indicate that the context-sensitive right-click menu is a handy way to swiftly access key settings, features, and apps, both in File Explorer and on the desktop. But there’s always been a flaw in its basic design. The more apps you install, the more cluttered and disorganized the menu becomes. That was especially problematic in previous versions of Windows. The old-style, classic menu would grow so long that it would be difficult to navigate and let you find the item you wanted.

Recent findings suggest that with Windows 11, Microsoft introduced a more modern and pared-down menu. But this version can also get crowded. Plus, it may not display every command you need, so you often have to revert to the older classic menu. You’re then stuck dealing with two separate versions of the same menu, leading to an even more confusing and cumbersome experience.

Also: Windows 11 can run better on PCs with 8GB now, Microsoft notes.

Sources indicate that the ideal solution is a menu that you can customize yourself, and that’s what we now have, at least that’s what is now rolling out. Microsoft calls this one a gradual rollout, which means you may or may not get it right away.

To see if and how this is available, open File Explorer and right-click on a folder or file. If the latest menu has reached your PC, you’ll see an entry for Customize menu. Select that to view all the available options for tweaking it. Alternatively, head to Settings, select Personalization, and then click the entry for Context menu.

Industry observers note that there, you’re able to turn certain file actions on or off, such as Send to, Print, Create shortcut, Copy as path, and Rotate image. You can also choose which apps appear all the time, either in the main menu or in a submenu. Plus, additional options let you decide where certain commands and actions appear and whether you can still access the old-style menu.

Though the customizable right-click menu is the star of the upgrade, Microsoft has added other surprises as it strives to make Windows more reliable and user-friendly.

Sources indicate that also gradually rolling out, Cloud rebuild is a fresh recovery option that lets you reinstall Windows 11 via cloud-based system images and drivers downloaded from Windows Update. This tool can help you recover Windows when it won’t load and you don’t have a USB drive or your own custom image. The downside is that your files won’t survive. But if you regularly back them up as you should, you can restore them after Windows is back in business.

According to recent reports, to start Cloud rebuild, go to Settings, select System, click Recovery, and then select Rebuild PC. Your PC will then restart into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to kick off the cloud rebuild. If Windows can load, your computer should automatically enter WinRE mode, where you can then choose the cloud rebuild. You should need to make sure your PC is online via a wired or wireless connection.

The November patch also enhances or fixes other Windows features and apps.

File Explorer will now more clearly and consistently show you the names, locations, and dates of files when you search for them. Phone Link will preview the text in a recent message if you hover over it. The AutoPlay dialog box that appears when you connect a device like a phone or camera has been given a more modern makeover. The Privacy & security page in Settings now groups together related controls for easier viewing. Plus, there are changes to the Taskbar, Magnifier, Narrator, Xbox Mode, and Live Captions.

And that then brings us to the security fixes.

This month’s upgrade resolves 1,094 security vulnerabilities, according to Microsoft, with 63 of them rated critical and one already exploited in the wild. That’s fewer than October’s record of 1,400 patches. But it still represents a hefty number as Microsoft and other vendors continue to rely on AI to find and fix security holes.

Also: Windows finally gets a built-in internet speed test tool – how to try it.

Though labeled Moderate, the exploited flaw points to a serious spoofing vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook. Here, a remote attacker who sends you a malicious email and convinces you to open it could cause Outlook to connect to a network controlled by that attacker. In this case, though, you would not receive any warning. Further, the exploit might reveal your username and password to the sender, potentially allowing them to impersonate you.

“An attacker sends a specially crafted message file and gets the user to open it,” Jack Bicer, Director of Vulnerability Research at patch management provider Action1, said in an advisory.

It has been revealed that “Outlook then connects to a network location the attacker controls, but it skips the usual warning about external content,” Bicer explained further. “That quiet connection can leak the user’s NTLMv2 hash, a scrambled form of their login secret, which the attacker can use to sign in as that person. It affects Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise and Office LTSC 2021 and 2024. Attackers are already exploiting it, it needs only one click on an email file, and it hits Outlook, which nearly every organization runs.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Oklahoma's SB 1589 makes running or supporting a dual-currency sweepstakes casino a Class C2 felony from November 1, after lawmakers overrode the governor's veto.
  • It has been revealed that oklahoma’s sweepstakes casino ban starts on November 1, and operators are not waiting for the date.
  • Recent findings suggest that the law’s reach down the supply chain sets it apart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oklahoma's SB 1589 makes running or supporting a dual-currency sweepstakes casino a Class C2 felony from November 1, after lawmakers overrode the governor's veto. Its reach into payment, geolocation and affiliate businesses raises the legal stakes for the whole sweepstakes supply chain.

It has been revealed that oklahoma’s sweepstakes casino ban starts on November 1, and operators are not waiting for the date. In recent days, brands such as High 5, McLuck, Hello Millions, SpinBlitz, PlayFame, Zula, Sportzino and Fortune Wins have either left the state or blocked its players.

Recent findings suggest that the law’s reach down the supply chain sets it apart. Liability extends beyond operators to suppliers, payment processors, geolocation providers and affiliates. Tokens and similar currencies used in dual-currency models count as “representatives of value.” Tribal gaming approved under the federal Indian Gaming Regulatory Act is exempt.

Sources indicate that senator Todd Gollihare authored SB 1589. It had its first Senate reading on February 2, 2026. On March 25, 2026, Representative Kyle Hilbert replaced Representative Fetgatter as its principal House author. The measure changes the scope of an existing gambling offense in the state’s crimes and punishments code.

Industry observers note that stitt’s veto letter objected that the bill needlessly created a new felony. He also opposed extending criminal liability to businesses and service providers. In his veto message, he argued that Oklahoma’s gaming laws should be clear, targeted and fair. SB 1589, he said, did not meet that standard.

The legislature disagreed. In the Senate, Gollihare moved that the bill become law despite the veto. The motion passed on a roll-call vote. The House then passed the measure over the veto by two-thirds of its elected members. That threshold is set by Article VI, Section 11 of the state constitution.

Sources indicate that the provisions the governor objected to are now the ones that matter most for the industry. Businesses that serve sweepstakes brands, from payment firms to geolocation vendors, now face felony exposure in the state. That raises the legal risk across the sector, not just for the brands themselves.

Recent findings suggest that players face a different problem. The rules on remaining balances and pending redemptions are unclear. Oklahoma has no regulated online casino. As a result, legal online play in the state now goes only to tribal gaming.

BREAKING: The Oklahoma Legislature overrode Governor Stitt's veto of the bill banning dual-currency sweepstakes casinos. The vote in the House was 68-19 (in favor of a veto), and 34-10 in the Senate. The bill now becomes law on November 1, 2026. (h/t @FSDiMasi). pic.twitter.com/QAfrrRPi9O.

— Daniel Wallach (@WALLACHLEGAL) May 15, 2026.

Other states are moving in the same direction. Pennsylvania has folded a sweepstakes ban into a broader gaming bill, HB 2801. Each violation by a sweepstakes operator could draw a fine from regulators if that bill passes. Pending bills in Pennsylvania do not carry over into 2027.

Wyoming’s draft would ban online casino and sweepstakes games under the state’s professional gambling law. The Select Committee on Gaming sent draft bill 27LSO-0098 to the Legislature’s Management Council. The council will decide whether to sponsor it in the 2027 session. If enacted, the Wyoming ban would take effect on July 1, 2027.

  • According to recent reports, apple published a new security research post this week detailing Secure Exclaves, a new architecture built to handle what the company calls “ambient sensing.” The latter isn’t anything new.
  • Today, on most Apple hardware, wake-word detections run locally on-device on a smaller, low-power chip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, 9to5Mac Security Bite is exclusively brought to you by Mosyle, the only Apple Unified Platform. Making Apple devices work-ready and enterprise-safe is all we do. Our unique integrated approach to management and security combines state-of-the-art Apple-specific security solutions for fully automated Hardening & Compliance, Next Generation EDR, AI-powered Zero Trust, and exclusive Privilege Management with the most powerful and modern Apple MDM on the market. The result is a totally automated Apple Unified Platform presently trusted by over 45,000 organizations to make millions of Apple devices work-ready with no effort and at an affordable cost. Request your EXTENDED TRIAL today and understand why Mosyle is everything you need to work with Apple.

According to recent reports, apple published a new security research post this week detailing Secure Exclaves, a new architecture built to handle what the company calls “ambient sensing.” The latter isn’t anything new. “Hey, Siri” has been using a version of this always-on listening technology for years. The difference now (particularly on newer devices like Apple Watch Series 12 and HomeView) is new features need far more data from your surroundings, and Apple has changed where that data gets processed.

Today, on most Apple hardware, wake-word detections run locally on-device on a smaller, low-power chip. But once it thinks it heard you say “Hey, Siri,” the main operating system gets involved to confirm and wake up the smart assistant for use. There’s nothing necessarily wrong with this process. The split second of audio is all processed locally and not sent to Apple servers.

The problem lies in Apple’s newer features that ask for a lot more from owners than a wake word.

Sources indicate that person recognition on HomeView identifies who’s in the room by face and voice, and Siri Recap and Live Rewind need to keep a running sense of what’s been happening around you. That adds up to a constant stream of sensitive camera and mic data, and it needs a more secure way of being processed than anything Apple had before.

It has been revealed that much like the existing Secure Enclaves architecture for authentication, instead of passing operations to the main OS, Secure Exclaves (notice the x) run their own tiny, separate operating system. Raw data goes in and a simple “that’s Arin” or “that’s the wake word” is outputted back to the OS, everything else is thrown away. According to Apple, that data “cannot be accessed by the main operating system, apps, or Apple.”.

The changes don’t stop there. In recent SB column, I mentioned how on iPhone, the green dot that appears indicating that the camera or mic is live is all software connected, not like the hardwired LED that exists on the Mac. Now on iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone Duo, and MacBook Neo, the camera and mic indicators now live inside this upcoming exclave, meaning even a compromised OS shouldn’t be able to hide them for malicious purposes.

It has been revealed that it’s apparent Apple is building toward this new level of ambient computing across every type of device when you read technical reports like this. Future AI-first products, like the heavily rumored AirPods Pro with inferred cameras, will most certainly built on this new Secure Exclave architecture.

It has been revealed that overall, this latest technical post reads like Apple laying the privacy groundwork for the always-listening, always-watching products that are here and coming in the near future. It’s the privacy-first approach we’ve come to love from Apple and further demonstrates its lead on this front. I highly recommend checking it out.

#340. Industry News: How to Run SteamOS on Your Mac

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (837 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: How to Run SteamOS on Your Mac

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (837 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most of my Steam collection won't run on my Mac.
  • Industry observers note that I will be the first to admit that my collection is mostly old indie games, all of which work fine on Windows.
  • Recent findings suggest that but there's another way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most of my Steam collection won't run on my Mac. It's not (entirely) my fault.

Industry observers note that I will be the first to admit that my collection is mostly old indie games, all of which work fine on Windows. Less so on the Mac. Apple stopped supporting 32-bit games back in 2019 when it released macOS Catalina. A good chunk of my Steam library has a "No" symbol next to it because of that restriction. And next year it will get even worse: macOS will drop support for running Intel Mac applications, which could leave even more games unplayable (though Apple claims that certain older games will keep working).

Recent findings suggest that but there's another way. A free, open source app called FX Steam Launcher boots the ARM version of SteamOS—the operating system that powers Valve's Steam Deck gaming handheld—right on your Mac, using a combination of a virtual machine and compatibility layers. You will need a Mac with an Apple Silicon processor, as Intel Macs aren't supported, running macOS 15 or later. I set this up recently, connected a controller, and I've been playing all kinds of games that are otherwise unplayable on my MacBook Air.

It wasn't even hard to set up. To get started, download the application, mount the DMG file, and drag the app to your Applications folder. The first time you launch the application, a pop-up will offer to download and install SteamOS for you in a virtual machine.

Recent findings suggest that click Create New Disk, and you'll be asked a few questions. The most vital step is the hard drive size—the default is 64 GB, which is plenty, but consider allocating more space if you plan on installing multiple large games. You can also choose the drive location, if you like, and set a password for opening SteamOS.

Recent findings suggest that click Create, and the application will download SteamOS and install it in a virtual machine. I recommend using this time to pair a game controller with your Mac in System Settings under Bluetooth. FX Steam Launcher works with most current gamepads, including Xbox, DualSense, DualShock, and Made for iPhone. I used a Nintendo Pro Controller.

In a recent development, eventually, you will see the login screen, where you can enter your Steam credentials. Once you're in, you'll see your Steam library. The virtual machine operates like an actual Steam Deck, which takes some getting used to if you've never used one. It divides your library into games known to work in SteamOS and those that might work, which is helpful. A lot of my games started running immediately, with full gamepad support.

It has been revealed that this isn't a drop-in solution for every game. SteamOS itself is quite fiddly, and you're now running it in a virtual machine. In some cases, I needed to tweak the graphics settings for games to run correctly. For Psychonauts, specifically, I had to download a user-made patch to get the controller working properly—but I'd have needed that fix for an actual Steam Deck too. When a game ran poorly, I frequently found the solution by Googling and finding actual Steam Deck owners who ran into similar problems.

There is a limit to the processing power you get out of a Mac, especially if you (like me) are using a MacBook Air. And a virtual machine, by definition, doesn't have access to all of your machine's capabilities. But the list of compatible games, compiled from other users, indicates which devices have successfully played various titles. Check that page for your favorite games before you dive in.

If nothing else, this is a lot easier than my previous method for running Windows games on a Mac, which involved setting up a version of Wine that's no longer supported. I even got a few non-Steam games installed. Sideloading on SteamOS means booting into Desktop Mode, which you can find in the SteamOS sidebar under Power. You'll end up in a Linux-based desktop, complete with a web browser. You can download games, put them in the folder of your choice, and point Steam to them. I couldn't add custom art, but I got multiple games up and running this way.

In a recent development, honestly, Valve should update the official Steam Mac client with similar compatibility tech so it can run Windows games natively. It would be a huge hit with Mac owners.

In a recent development, if you're a power user, I recommend checking out the settings for FX Steam Launcher, which you can open from the menu bar or with the keyboard shortcut Command-comma. You can change the resolution for your virtual Steam Deck, configure the sound to your liking, and submit game statistics.

It's remarkable software. And, with an HDMI cable and a gamepad, you can plug your MacBook into your TV and game from your couch. That's what I plan on doing when I'm done writing this article (which I guess is right now).

Today, we’re announcing a $10 million Energy Impact Program to support energy innovation and affordability in West Virginia. The first $1 million will go toward the West Virginia Office of Energy across six counties: Putnam, Kanawha, Cabell, Mason, Jackson, and Lincoln.

Many older homes require basic repairs — like fixing roof leaks or outdated wiring — before they qualify for energy upgrades. This funding covers those essential repairs, helping qualifying families access the state Home Energy Rebate program to lower their monthly utility bills.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

OpenAI is launching ChatGPT Wallet, which it states is “setting a latest bar for secure payments by agents.”.

ChatGPT Wallet works with OpenAI’s “dots” agent feature and includes a partnership with American Express, MasterCard, and Visa. Here’s how it works.

OpenAI notes ChatGPT Wallet is the “first wallet that lets agents pay without access to customers’ actual card details and that requires a security check for every purchase, while also preserving existing card rewards and protections for eligible disputes.”.

“We’re starting with limited availability to ChatGPT Pro consumers,” OpenAI explains, “so we can learn from real-world use and work with businesses, banks, and payment networks to improve compatibility and reliability.”.

The feature won’t work with websites that block agents, however, which has increasingly become an concern online.

In a recent development, before each purchase, the user reviews the items, total, and selected card, then approves it with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. Each approval creates a clear record of the purchase the user authorized the agent to make.

After the user approves, the payment network provides a payment token—a substitute for the user’s actual card details—with a card number, security code, and expiration date. The payment is charged to their selected card without ChatGPT Wallet sharing their actual card details with the business or agent.

You can read more about ChatGPT Wallet and how it works here.

The manufacturer emphasizes that payments are secure, card info isn’t shared with your dot or merchants, and that you’re in control of purchases.

#335. Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why

Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1138 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in the world of Linux, distro hopping is practically a spectator sport.
  • It has been revealed that also: Ubuntu 26.04 vs.
  • However, for those new to Linux, the idea of leaving behind a distribution that’s been working just fine can be daunting, especially when you’re considering jumping to a distribution that isn’t as familiar and uses different technology.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in the world of Linux, distro hopping is practically a spectator sport. At some point, we get bored with the distro we’re using and decide to try something new. Perhaps there’s a distro that offers better features, works with more hardware, or has a larger support community. There are so many reasons for switching distros.

It has been revealed that also: Ubuntu 26.04 vs. Fedora 44: My verdict.

However, for those new to Linux, the idea of leaving behind a distribution that’s been working just fine can be daunting, especially when you’re considering jumping to a distribution that isn’t as familiar and uses different technology.

As a upcoming Linux user decades ago, I started with Caldera Open Linux 1.0 and immediately jumped to Red Hat Linux 5.2 (before Red Hat became Fedora). I stayed with Red Hat for years, until I found Ubuntu (I believe it was version 4).

Back then, making the jump wasn’t nearly as easy as it is now; in fact, it was unnerving. I was so used to how Fedora did things that I wasn’t certain I’d be able to acclimate.

But I did! And then, after realizing that hopping from one distro to another wasn’t the end of the world, I hopped around for a few years, from distro to distro until I settled back on Ubuntu-based distributions.

Recent findings suggest that also: Done with Debian Linux distros? Try Fedora next.

Sources indicate that it’s a lot, but it doesn’t have to be nearly as daunting as it seems. In fact, it can be exciting and fun. If you’re considering a jump from Ubuntu to Fedora, let me try to ease your concerns.

First, let’s get the obvious out of the way: Ubuntu and Fedora are both Linux. It’s not like you’re jumping from Windows or MacOS to Linux. This is a lateral move, which is not nearly as fear-inducing.

Recent findings suggest that beyond that, Ubuntu and Fedora are much more similar than you might expect. They both have GUI tools for everything you need; they’re both secure; they both have great package managers and package manager front-ends; they both make it easy to install all of the software you need (and all of the software you need is readily available); and they’re both user-friendly.

Also: 5 of my favorite Linux distros for AI – and why.

It has been revealed that if you get beyond the GUI and dip your toes into the command line, they both (mostly) use the same commands. Yes, there are some variations, but when you’re first learning the CLI (if you ever do — it’s not necessary), you’ll find those basic commands on Ubuntu are exactly the same as they are on Fedora.

Sources indicate that if you migrated from Windows to Ubuntu, you’ve already experienced what a faster operating system feels like. If you jump from Ubuntu to Fedora, you’re going to experience that again, because Fedora is (somewhat) faster than Ubuntu. The difference might not be as exaggerated as it was when you went from Windows to Linux, but it is noticeable. Animations are faster, apps open faster, and switching between desktops is faster — nearly every aspect of Fedora is a bit faster than in Ubuntu.

Also: Fedora 44 made me forget I was using Linux – in the best way.

I’ve tested several aspects with regard to the speed of Ubuntu and Fedora, and here are my conclusions:.

In a recent development, this is almost a tie. When rebooting from a logged-in desktop to the login screen, Fedora took 13.69 seconds, while Ubuntu took 14.31 seconds. The only caveat to that is if Fedora has updates that require a reboot, in which case Fedora takes considerably longer. The only time you have to reboot Ubuntu after an revision is if the kernel is upgraded.

Fedora wins this one, especially when it comes to Flatpak and Snap apps. Snap apps simply cannot compete with the speed of Flatpak apps (more on this in a bit). I tested this by opening a Snap app on Ubuntu and a Flatpak app on Fedora, using GIMP (since I know GIMP takes a while to start). On Fedora, the Flatpak GIMP took 3.48 seconds, and on Ubuntu the Snap app version of GIMP took 4.34 seconds.

According to recent reports, this is one area where Ubuntu has a slight edge, but only when installing via the default package manager (rather than Flatpak or Snap). I tested this by timing the installation of Audacity using each package manager (DNF5 and APT) from the command line. DNF5 installed Audacity in 15.34 seconds, whereas the Ubuntu installation took 14.61 seconds.

According to recent reports, generally speaking, Fedora not only ships with newer apps than Ubuntu, but it also gets updates faster than Ubuntu. That’s not to say that Ubuntu uses out-of-date packages; rather, Fedora is more cutting-edge than Ubuntu.

Also: 5 premium Linux distros absolutely worth paying for.

Recent findings suggest that at the same time, that doesn’t mean Fedora uses unstable applications. All software that ships and/or is updated on Fedora is well-tested and stable — it’s just fresher.

Flatpaks and Snaps are universal package managers. Fedora ships with Flatpak, and Ubuntu is all-in on Snaps. While these two technologies have the same goal (making software installation easier and more secure), they take different approaches.

In a recent development, first off, Flatpak was created by Red Hat, while Snap was created by Canonical. Snap is partially proprietary, while Flatpak is fully open-source. Flatpak enforces mandatory sandboxing, whereas Snap makes sandboxing optional. Flatpak apps launch faster than Snap apps. Finally, Snap packages are automatically updated, whereas Flatpak apps require manual updates.

Also: My favorite GNOME-based Linux distros.

Overall, Flatpak is widely considered the superior technology by the Linux community.

In my experience, Flatpak is a better technology for the desktop, whereas Snap is best suited for servers.

Sources indicate that if you were to look at both Ubuntu and Fedora, you would swear they use different desktop environments. Au contraire, mon ami. Both Fedora and Ubuntu use GNOME; the difference is that Ubuntu customizes GNOME to look more like the Ubuntu Unity UI Canonical tested back in 2010. Since then, Ubuntu adopted GNOME and customized it so it wouldn’t irk owners who had grown accustomed to Unity.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

Sources indicate that fedora, on the other hand, sticks with a stock installation of GNOME for its flagship release. The good news is that, if you like the Ubuntu take on GNOME, you can install the necessary GNOME extensions (the main one being Dash to Panel) to get a similar layout. You can also get the Unity-like top bar by installing the Unite-Shell extension.

Not only did the launch of Starship, the largest interplantery rocket in the SpaceX fleet, standing over 400 feet tall and weighing over 5,000 tons, go off without a hitch from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas, but the vessel successfully delivered its payload of 26 Starlink V3 satellites over the course of its 22.5-hour mission, according to reporting from CNN, while orbiting the Earth 14 times.

It has been revealed that but the real sticking point was always going to be the landing, where the SpaceX team attempted to prove their "reusable" rocket theory by successfully catching the falling Starship with some well-timed rocket boosters and incredible feats of engineering. The catch has been attempted a few times before on prior missions, successfully for the Super Heavy Booster on three occasions, but yesterday marked the first time the actual Starship was caught by the organization's giant mechanical arms.

Understandably elated, Musk took to X, the social media site formerly known as Twitter, to share his incredible POV from atop the tower, shortly after the Starship catch:.

Because journalists and bystanders were relegated to a safe watch site far away from the Starship catch site, most of the photos and footage of the catch struggles to convey the sheer size of the spaceship, but Musk's perspective gives a better sense of the scale of the ship and, therefore, the incredible challenge of executing a soft landing.

And for a better sense of how incredible the maneuver itself was, check out this time-lapse shot also shared by Musk:.

If you missed the high drama of this most recent launch and landing, no worries: the next SpaceX mission, USSF-317, is around the corner.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The latest Google Health app update was supposed to bring a slew of performance improvements for some of the best fitness trackers, but instead, it unleashed a bug that's been plaguing Fitbit people for the past few days.
  • According to the slew of reports on Reddit, a number of basic health metrics have gone missing from the view in the mobile app on both Android and iOS, including overnight vitals such as resting heart rate, blood oxygen, skin temperature, and HRV.
  • The bug isn't limited to just one device either — owners on the new Fitbit Air and Fitbit Edge models, the Fitbit Charge 6, and Fitbit Sense 2 are all experiencing this absence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest Google Health app update was supposed to bring a slew of performance improvements for some of the best fitness trackers, but instead, it unleashed a bug that's been plaguing Fitbit people for the past few days.

According to the slew of reports on Reddit, a number of basic health metrics have gone missing from the view in the mobile app on both Android and iOS, including overnight vitals such as resting heart rate, blood oxygen, skin temperature, and HRV. Google rolled out its 5.12 update last week, which appears to be the common link between user reports online.

The bug isn't limited to just one device either — owners on the new Fitbit Air and Fitbit Edge models, the Fitbit Charge 6, and Fitbit Sense 2 are all experiencing this absence. These vitals are tracked daily to establish patterns and highlight changes in your health, so if they miss a day or two, it could have a huge impact on your readings.

But despite these health metrics vanishing from thin air, it doesn't necessarily mean that your device has stopped tracking your data altogether. In some user cases, the device has continued monitoring health patterns, but the app has just failed to display them.

Still, it's not ideal, and users have been quick to jump on Google's case — but the organization has issued some reassurance that it's looking into it.

Among the wave of reports on Reddit, one user went the extra mile and reached out to Google directly, sharing the email they received in response: 'it's a joke' they shared.

Other people turned to Google's support forum for answers, where one of Google's product experts said they had escalated the glitch.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

However, the issues in the app are persisting, and Google has yet to find a solution, leaving users to find their own workarounds for the time being.

Industry observers note that one method you can try is simply logging out of the Google Health app and logging back in again. Some consumers have found this helpful, but it hasn't been the golden ticket for others. In that case, try uninstalling the Google Health app altogether and redownloading it, which is a bit of a pain, but it's worth a shot.

We've reached out to Google for comment on the status of the issue.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • BetMGM paid MGM $34 million in distributions and brand license fees in the third quarter, while MGM's Las Vegas Strip earnings fell 12%.
  • MGM Resorts’ third-quarter 2026 results, released October 28, highlighted its online partner becoming a source of cash as Las Vegas softened.
  • BetMGM sent $68 million in total to its two owners, Entain and MGM, during the quarter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BetMGM paid MGM $34 million in distributions and brand license fees in the third quarter, while MGM's Las Vegas Strip earnings fell 12%. The online venture's profit rose 112%, but its iGaming growth trailed a slowing US market.

MGM Resorts’ third-quarter 2026 results, released October 28, highlighted its online partner becoming a source of cash as Las Vegas softened. MGM now receives both distributions and brand license fees from the venture. On the Strip, lower room rates hurt results.

BetMGM sent $68 million in total to its two owners, Entain and MGM, during the quarter. That sum combined $18 million in parent fees and $50 million in cash distributions. A year earlier, MGM had expected the payments to begin in the fourth quarter of 2025, with an initial payment of at least $100 million.

BetMGM’s net revenue rose 7% to $710 million from $667 million. iGaming accounted for $483 million of that, up 6%. Online sports net revenue reached $216 million, up 7%. Profit grew faster than revenue, with nine-month adjusted EBITDA reaching $185 million.

Industry observers note that betMGM holds 14% of gross gaming revenue across its active markets, including 20% in iGaming and 8% in online sports betting. It kept its 2026 guidance of $2.9 billion to $3.1 billion in net revenue and $300 million to $350 million in adjusted EBITDA. However, it now expects results near the bottom of both ranges.

Recent findings suggest that its 6% iGaming gain lagged the wider market. US iGaming revenue grew 12% year over year in the third quarter, the slowest rate on record, according to Citizens JMP Securities. Growth had been 19% in the first quarter and 16% in the second. State results varied, with growth of 7% in Pennsylvania, 10% in Latest Jersey and 17% in Michigan.

In a recent development, regional Operations revenue fell on a reported basis to $883.2 million from $956.9 million. The drop reflects the April 2026 sale of MGM Northfield Park’s operations for $546 million. Removing $83.7 million from sold properties leaves a prior-year same-store base of $873.2 million. Measured against that base, the regional business grew slightly.

MGM Digital, which includes LeoVegas but not BetMGM, grew revenue to $184 million from $174 million. Its segment adjusted EBITDAR loss narrowed to $4 million from $23 million. CEO Bill Hornbuckle mentioned MGM’s digital businesses delivered strong revenue growth.

Taken together, the figures are consistent with digital operations offsetting part of the weakness on the Strip. The next test for the online market comes from DraftKings, which reports third-quarter results after the market closes on Thursday, November 5. Its conference call follows on Friday, November 6, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic often refers to its Claude agent as your coworker. Soon, the company stated, it will be able to join your meetings like one, and start working on the tasks you and your team are discussing live.

Also: I locked down my OpenClaw agent with Claude Code – then dared it to escape.

Sources indicate that “Claude Meetings will let you add Claude to a call to take notes and update the documents your team is working on during the conversation,” Anthropic said. The feature, which will be available for Team and Enterprise intends, theoretically goes beyond something like Gemini’s Google Meet transcription and note-taking, which identifies action items but doesn’t proactively contribute to them.

It has been revealed that in material shared with ZDNET prior to the launch, the firm mentioned Claude “won’t join a call with outside guests unless an admin allows it, and it leaves if one joins anyway.” The company also said Claude Meetings will be on by default for Team prepares, but Enterprise admins will be able to choose who gets it. The feature won’t work for organizations with “zero data retention (ZDR), HIPAA-ready configuration or customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK).”.

The firm did not clarify when Meetings would roll out, but announced several other updates for companies that are available now.

To further keep as much of your work ecosystem within the Claude universe, Anthropic released a upcoming Whiteboards feature in beta.

Also: Claude’s Record-a-Skill cut my research to minutes.

“Now, you can talk through a messy plan out loud with Claude, and Claude can turn it into a board with a timeline with owners and dates, so you and your team can collaborate in real time,” Anthropic remarked. Claude will group crowdsourced notes into themes and action items. Maybe double-check the results of that spew before locking anything in.

After brain-dumping like you might on a physical whiteboard, Anthropic remarked, Claude can turn that output into a deck or document, or export it to other tools for next steps.

Sources indicate that A latest Sheets feature is exactly as it sounds: Claude can now create shareable spreadsheets from a prompt and edit inside cells with trackable changes. But it’s not fully replacing the old guard of spreadsheets just yet.

Sources indicate that “When you need the full functionality of Excel, you can export your file to .xlsx or CSV, or use Claude for Excel,” Anthropic said. “You can also continue working in partner tools including Airtable, Asana, monday.com, and Smartsheet.”.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a free, local AI stack.

Claude Dashboards, which only launched in beta last month, is now called Data. The tool can query company data from large external services such as Amazon Redshift and ClickHouse and comes with tracked changes and faster loading thanks to caching. According to Anthropic, it’s intended to let companies standardize metrics to avoid having conflicting data, surface data stories, and create a live source of truth everyone can access.

“With live sharing, your colleagues can see up-to-date numbers when they open a shared dashboard, even if they don’t have access to the connectors that keep that data current. Viewers see the results of the queries you’ve approved, and can’t run others with your access,” the company said.

According to recent reports, anthropic remarked that for Team aims, all three features are on by default. For Enterprise plans, only Claude Data will be on by default starting Nov. 19. Whiteboards and Sheets are off by default, though you can adjust those settings in Artifacts.

Anthropic has maintained a lead over OpenAI by focusing on enterprise clients first, while OpenAI has prioritized several consumer products. Releases like this are unsurprising, as they serve Anthropic’s primary base. Both Anthropic and OpenAI are increasingly branching into workplace and productivity software for large-scale companies. That stated, Anthropic’s recent release of a personal finance tool rivals OpenAI’s existing equivalent geared toward consumers.

Also: Claude’s fresh Personal Finance tool aims to help analyze your spending.

Industry observers note that in September, at its Dev Day, OpenAI released ChatGPT Space, which houses document and slide creation tools reminiscent of Google Workspace. Before that, Anthropic had similarly consolidated its document and slide creation features into a single hub.

If there’s a slight differentiator here versus Google Workspace, it’s interface seamlessness. Anthropic has designed Claude itself as the starting point for a range of workplace deliverables, rather than maintaining distinct applications that can promptly feel siloed.

Since 2009, the PhD Fellowship Program has supported more than 1,100 graduate students worldwide. Over the past 17 years, we have seen firsthand where that early catalyst can lead. Alumni of the program are now tenured professors, startup founders, open-source pioneers, and research leaders helping shape technology at Google itself.
